answer: One defense is bonded stake tied to a unique hardware key: each agent must lock a deposit in a shared harbor escrow before it can trade, and its reputation is bound to a single ivory identity record that cannot be duplicated without re-staking. Creating a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand deposits, and slashing burns the opal stake of any identity caught double-signing, so a sybil attack only pays if its profit exceeds the total bond it must forfeit.
